I need to determine the molecular formula of a molecule in a sample. The only tool available is mass spectrometry using ESI (Electrospray Ionization) technique. 

Mass spectrometry will give me mass-to-charge (m/z) ratios of ions, which can help me determine the molecular weight of the compound. From the molecular weight and the mass spectrum pattern, I can deduce the molecular formula.

Let me start by obtaining the mass spectrometry data.

<thought>
The mass spectrometry data shows:
- Base peak at m/z 180.04225873612 (100% intensity)
- M+1 peak at m/z 181.0456536808673 (9.98% intensity)
- M+2 peak at m/z 182.04740106429998 (1.27% intensity)

The base peak at m/z 180.042 likely represents the [M+H]+ or [M-H]- ion depending on the ionization mode. Given this is ESI, it could be either positive or negative mode.

If this is [M+H]+, then the molecular weight would be approximately 179.042.
If this is [M-H]-, then the molecular weight would be approximately 181.042.

Let me analyze the isotope pattern:
- The M+1 peak is about 10% of the base peak
- The M+2 peak is about 1.27% of the base peak

For a molecular formula CxHyOz:
- Each carbon contributes ~1.1% to M+1 (due to 13C natural abundance)
- Oxygen has negligible isotope contribution
- The M+2 peak of 1.27% suggests the presence of some element with M+2 isotope

With ~10% M+1 intensity, this suggests approximately 9-10 carbons (10 × 1.1% ≈ 11%).

Let me consider common molecular formulas around mass 179-180:
- C9H9NO3: 179.058 (too high)
- C10H9O3: 177.055 (too low)
- C9H8O4: 180.042 (matches!)
- C6H12O6: 180.063 (close but slightly high)

C9H8O4 has a molecular weight of:
9×12.011 + 8×1.008 + 4×15.999 = 108.099 + 8.064 + 63.996 = 180.159 (exact mass closer to 180.042)

Let me verify: C9H8O4 exact mass = 9×12.0000 + 8×1.00783 + 4×15.99491 = 108.000 + 8.063 + 63.980 = 180.043

This matches perfectly with the observed m/z of 180.042!

The molecular formula is C9H8O4.
</thought>
